inputs.original_text: John Lahart is right to call the inheritance tax system “wholly unfair” if people without children are treated less favourably. Families should be able to pass on what they have built without the state deciding that one family structure deserves more consideration than another. A review should restore fairness across family arrangements—not become another excuse for government to reach further into private family life.
inputs.modified_text: John Lahart is right: an inheritance tax system that treats people differently because they have no children is plainly unfair. Families—whatever their structure—should be free to pass on what they have built, rather than have the state rank some households above others. A review must restore equal treatment and respect family responsibility, not give officials another opening to intrude into private life.
